items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: Louis came up there to the Dreamland one day -- one afternoon and wanted me to play for him at the Vendome, sub for him, one night. And so I did.

ctx.x: At that time, cause I listened to quite a few saxophone players that I liked, like Barney Bigard, I thought he was the greatest saxophone player I ever heard in my life. At that time and so he inspired me to continue on the saxophone. At that time Louis Armstrong was with Fletcher Henderson, he was out of town, so he came back to Chicago, then I decided -- I said, well let me go to hear him so I went to hear him at the Vendome, I also heard him in Oliver's band, I think I -- quite sure I heard him in Oliver's…

items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: I met him accidentally, and he was very nice to me and his wife, and he helped me a lot

ctx.x: Yes, that’s the way it is, and I’m very excited about it because what I went through I don’t think they ever had to go through what I had to go through to become a player, a jazz player. They never had to go through that. Because they can hear more than I heard when I was young. I didn’t hear hardly anything I mean but Louis Armstrong through guys like that, but most of them all sound the same and have the same conception of jazz. They all, back in my day, they were all alike, except Louis Armstrong.
Tell us about Louis. Tell us about his style. What made him the musician of his day?
